text.p: The Palestinian legislature voted unanimously on Saturday to begin drafting a military conscription law, Council Speaker Ahmed Korei said.
The decision was taken against the background of heightened tensions with Israel over the killing by two Islamic suicide bombers of 13 people in a Jerusalem market on July 30.
"The Council has voted unanimously in favour of drafting a military service law," Korei, also known as Abu Ala, told a news conference.
He said the legislature's legal committee would be asked to prepare the law for final approval by the Palestinian Authority, led by President Yasser Arafat.
Legislator Azmi Shoaibi said he had initiated the proposal, under which Palestinian university graduates would be inducted into "military and public service" for a period of six months to a year.
He also said youths would receive training to enable them "to defend the Palestinian people".
Under Israeli-PLO interim peace deals the self-rule administration in the West Bank and Gaza is in charge of a police force, armed with automatic weapons, and several security agencies.
